correctness.rationale: Exact prime-power factors (1,1+p^-2,1+p^-2+p^-4) and Euler product zeta(2)/zeta(6) give global maximum. The crucial complete prime-tail interval is proved by 7 explicitly verified strict rational inequalities for p<29 and Nagura prime gaps for p>=29, plus a valid three-choice interval-covering recursion. Nine local p=2,3 multiplier intervals are exhaustively ordered; Archimedean rational pi bounds certify the two strict gaps and all requisite overlaps. Cube-free valuation CRT/Mobius density computation yields 36/91,16/91,39/91 summing to one. Actual verify.py replay passes with exact rational certificate; its finite enumeration is illustrative and not offered as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Defant identified exact component counts for exponent-restricted generalized divisor images as a mathematical gap. The first nonsquarefree exponent cutoff, k=2, r=2, has a complete three-interval closure with exact endpoints and componentwise cube-free densities, not just an approximation or arbitrary slice. It establishes a meaningful stability phenomenon relative to the unrestricted 3-component case, and its proof isolates the general mechanism of a continuous large-prime Euler-product tail. No general theorem for other cutoffs or exponents is claimed.
